stimuli.title: Eight persons — Ananya, Geeta, Deepak, Bhavna, Ojas, Farhan, Charu, and Tushar — live in an eight-flat four-storey building. The bottom floor is 1 and the top floor is 4. Each floor has two flats: Flat A and Flat B. Flat A is to the west of Flat B.
stimuli.body:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions that follow:
• There is exactly one floor between the floors of Farhan and Tushar, and both live in Flat B.
• The number of floors above Tushar is equal to the number of floors below Deepak.
• Tushar lives on Floor 2 in Flat B.
• Farhan lives immediately above Charu in the same flat.
• Geeta lives on an even numbered floor in Flat A.
• The number of floors above Geeta is equal to the number of floors below Charu.
• Ojas lives immediately to the west of Farhan.
• Tushar lives immediately above Bhavna in the same flat.
• Ananya lives on Floor 1 in Flat A.

(Note: Flat A is immediately to the west of Flat B on each floor).
stimuli.solution: Floor 4: Flat A = Ojas, Flat B = Farhan | Floor 3: Flat A = Deepak, Flat B = Charu | Floor 2: Flat A = Geeta, Flat B = Tushar | Floor 1: Flat A = Ananya, Flat B = Bhavna

stimuli.title: Eight persons — Sana, Yash, Deepak, Ojas, Himanshu, Kunal, Harish, and Esha — sit around a circular table. Four of them face the center and four face away from the center (outside).
stimuli.body:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions that follow:
• Yash sits diametrically opposite to Deepak.
• Harish sits immediately to the right of Ojas.
• Ojas sits immediately to the left of Yash.
• Kunal sits second to the left of Himanshu.
• Sana sits second to the left of Deepak.
• Kunal sits immediately to the right of Sana.
• Esha sits at Seat 6 facing the outside.

(Note: Positions are numbered 1 to 8 consecutively in a clockwise direction).
stimuli.solution: Seat 1: Sana (facing Center), Seat 2: Himanshu (facing Outside), Seat 3: Yash (facing Center), Seat 4: Ojas (facing Outside), Seat 5: Harish (facing Center), Seat 6: Esha (facing Outside), Seat 7: Deepak (facing Center), Seat 8: Kunal (facing Outside)

stimuli.title: Eight persons — Geeta, Ojas, Bharat, Farhan, Himanshu, Nikhil, Zara, and Varun — have their preliminary examinations scheduled on two different dates (7th and 21st) across four months (March, April, May, and June).
stimuli.body:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions that follow:
• Geeta attends the exam on 7th of a month having 31 days.
• Zara attends the exam immediately after Nikhil.
• The number of persons attending the exam before Varun is equal to the number of persons attending after Nikhil.
• Only one person attends the exam between Zara and Himanshu.
• Only one person attends the exam between Geeta and Nikhil.
• Varun attends the exam in March.
• Farhan attends the exam on 7th of a month having 31 days.
• The number of persons attending the exam before Ojas is equal to the number of persons attending after Geeta.
• Bharat attends the exam on 7th April.

(Note: The order of months is March, April, May, and June. Each month has exams on the 7th and 21st).
stimuli.solution: March 7th: Farhan; March 21th: Varun; April 7th: Bharat; April 21th: Ojas; May 7th: Geeta; May 21th: Himanshu; June 7th: Nikhil; June 21th: Zara

stimuli.title: Ten persons sit in two parallel rows containing five persons each, such that there is equal distance between adjacent persons. In Row 1: A, B, C, D, and E sit facing South. In Row 2: P, Q, R, S, and T sit facing North.
stimuli.body:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions that follow:
• S sits to the immediate left of Q.
• Q sits to the immediate left of T.
• P sits second to the right of Q. 
• A sits at one of the extreme ends of Row 1.
• R sits to the immediate right of P.
• E sits second to the left of D.
• D sits directly opposite to S.
• B sits second to the left of C.

(Note: Each person in Row 1 faces a person in Row 2 directly opposite to them).
stimuli.solution: Row 1 (South): D - C - E - B - A | Row 2 (North): S - Q - T - P - R

stimuli.title: Caselet: Student enrollment in competitive exam streams
stimuli.body:
Read the passage carefully to answer the following questions:
In an institute of 600 aspirants, students opted for coaching across three exam streams: Banking, SSC, and Railways.
• 120 students opted ONLY for Banking.
• 150 students opted ONLY for SSC.
• 100 students opted ONLY for Railways.
• 50 students opted for BOTH Banking and SSC, but not Railways.
• 40 students opted for BOTH SSC and Railways, but not Banking.
• 60 students opted for BOTH Banking and Railways, but not SSC.
• 30 students opted for ALL THREE exam streams.
The remaining students did not opt for any of these three streams.

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few books are papers.
• All papers are notes.
• No notes is a diaries.

Conclusions:
I. Some books are not papers.
II. No papers is a diaries.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few books are papers' implies both 'Some books are papers' and 'Some books are NOT papers'. Thus, Conclusion I definitely follows.
2. Since all papers are inside notes and no notes is a diaries, there is no intersection between papers and diaries. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few books are papers.
• Few papers are notes.
• All notes are diaries.

Conclusions:
I. All books being papers is a possibility.
II. Some papers are diaries.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few books are papers' strictly forbids all books from being papers. Hence, Conclusion I is NOT a valid possibility.
2. Since some papers are notes and all notes are diaries, the common portion of papers and notes must also be diaries. Hence, Conclusion II definitely follows.

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Some books are papers.
• No papers is a notes.
• All notes are diaries.

Conclusions:
I. Some books can never be notes.
II. All papers being diaries is a possibility.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
1. The elements of books that are papers cannot be notes because no papers is a notes. Hence, 'Some books can never be notes' follows.
2. There is no negative restriction between papers and diaries. Hence, all papers being diaries is a valid possibility. Both follow.

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few books are papers.
• Some papers are notes.
• All notes are diaries.

Conclusions:

options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: P > Q ≥ R = S; T ≤ U < R; W ≥ P

Conclusions: I. W > S    II. P > T
options: Both conclusions I and II are true
Either conclusion I or II is true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• W ≥ P > Q ≥ R = S ⇒ W > S (Conclusion I is definitely true).
• P > R and R > U ≥ T ⇒ P > T (Conclusion II is definitely true).
Both conclusions I and II are true.

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: A ≥ B > C = D; E < F ≤ C; G > B

Conclusions: I. G > E    II. A ≥ F
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• G > B > C ≥ F > E ⇒ G > E (Conclusion I is true).
• A ≥ B > C ≥ F ⇒ A > F, so A ≥ F is not definitely true. (Conclusion II is false).

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: K ≤ L < M = N; O ≥ P > L; Q ≤ K

Conclusions: I. O > K    II. N > Q
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• O ≥ P > L > K ⇒ O > K (Conclusion I is true).
• N = M > L > K ≥ Q ⇒ N > Q (Conclusion II is true).
Both conclusions are true.

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: H > I < J ≤ K; L ≤ M < I; N ≥ K

Conclusions: I. H > M    II. L > N
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• H > I and M > I: signs between H and M oppose. (Conclusion I cannot be definitely established).
• L ≤ M < I < J ≤ K ≤ N: L < N, not L > N. (Conclusion II is false).
Therefore, neither conclusion is true.

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: V ≥ W > X = Y; Z ≤ Y; U < V

Conclusions: I. W < Z    II. V > X
options: Both conclusions I and II are true
Either conclusion I or II is true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• W > X = Y ≥ Z ⇒ W > Z (so W < Z is false).
• V ≥ W > X ⇒ V > X (Conclusion II is definitely true).

questions.stem:
Study the information carefully to answer the questions:
A family consists of seven members: P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V spanning three generations. There are two married couples.
• P is the paternal grandfather of V.
• Q is the only son of P.
• R is the daughter-in-law of P and mother of V.
• S is the sister of Q.
• T is the sister-in-law of R and is unmarried.
• U is the husband of S and father of a daughter.

How is Q related to V?
questions.explanation: P is the grandfather of V, and Q is the only son of P. R is the mother of V and wife of Q. Therefore, Q is the father of V.

questions.stem: How is S related to V?
questions.explanation: S is the sister of Q (V's father). Therefore, S is V's father's sister, which is Paternal Aunt.

questions.stem: How is U related to Q?
questions.explanation: U is the husband of S, who is Q's sister. Therefore, U is Q's sister's husband (Brother-in-law).

questions.stem: A person starts walking from Point A, walks 12 meters towards North to reach Point B. He then turns right (East) and walks 9 meters to reach Point C. He then turns right (South) and walks 12 meters to reach Point D. In which direction and at what shortest distance is Point D from Point A?
questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 12m North − 12m South = 0m. Net East displacement = 9m East. Hence, Point D is exactly 9 meters East of Point A.

1. B(2) - A(1): B, A (1 pair backward)
2. I(9) - N(14): I J K L M N (1 pair forward). Total = 2 pairs.

questions.stem: What is the ratio of the total number of male employees in Branch A and Branch C together to the total number of female employees in Branch B and Branch D together?
questions.explanation:
Male in A = 180, Male in C = 300. Total males (A+C) = 480.
Female in B = 160, Female in D = 180. Total females (B+D) = 340.
Ratio = 480 : 340 = 24:17.

questions.stem: The number of male employees in Branch B is what percent more or less than the number of female employees in Branch E?
questions.explanation:
Male in B = 200, Female in E = 180.
Difference = 200 − 180 = 20.
Percentage = (20 / 180) × 100% = 11.1% (more).

questions.stem: What is the average number of female employees working across all the five branches?
questions.explanation:
Total female employees = 60 + 160 + 180 + 180 + 180 = 760.
Average = 760 ÷ 5 = 152.

questions.stem: Find the difference between the total number of male employees in Branches C, D, and E together and the total number of female employees in Branches A, B, and C together.
questions.explanation:
Total males (C+D+E) = 300 + 120 + 240 = 660.
Total females (A+B+C) = 60 + 160 + 180 = 400.
Difference = 660 − 400 = 260.

questions.stem: If in another Branch F, the total number of employees is 25% more than that in Branch A, and the ratio of Male to Female employees in Branch F is 3 : 2, find the number of male employees in Branch F.
questions.explanation:
Total in Branch A = 240.
Total in Branch F = 240 × 1.25 = 300.
Male in Branch F = (3 / 5) × 300 = 180.

questions.stem: What is the total number of unsold units in January, February, and April taken together?

questions.stem: What is the average number of units sold per month by the company over the given five months?
Find the simplest ratio of the unsold units in May to the sold units in February.

Unsold in May = 900 − 765 = 135.

questions.stem: If each sold unit earns ₹1,500 and each unsold unit incurs a storage penalty of ₹200, what is the net earnings of the company in January?
questions.explanation:
Revenue from sold units = 420 × ₹1,500 = ₹6,30,000.
Storage penalty for unsold units = 80 × ₹200 = ₹16,000.
Net earnings = ₹6,30,000 − ₹16,000 = ₹614,000.

In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 ⇒ y = 4, 5.
Comparing roots:
• 7 > 4 and 7 > 5
• 8 > 4 and 8 > 5
Hence, x > y.

questions.stem:
In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 5x + 6 = 0
Equation II: y² − 13y + 42 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 5x + 6 = 0 ⇒ (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 ⇒ x = 2, 3.
For Eq II: y² − 13y + 42 = 0 ⇒ (y − 6)(y − 7) = 0 ⇒ y = 6, 7.
Comparing roots:
• 2 < 6 and 2 < 7
• 3 < 6 and 3 < 7
Hence, x < y.

questions.stem:

Equation II: y² − 13y + 42 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 3x − 10 = 0
Equation II: y² − 7y + 12 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 3x − 10 = 0 ⇒ (x − 5)(x + 2) = 0 ⇒ x = 5, −2.
For Eq II: y² − 7y + 12 = 0 ⇒ (y − 3)(y − 4) = 0 ⇒ y = 3, 4.
Comparing roots:
• When x = 5: 5 > 3 and 5 > 4 (x > y)
• When x = −2: −2 < 3 and −2 < 4 (x < y)
Since opposite relationships hold, relationship cannot be established.

What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following number series?
12, 7, 9, 16.5, 37, ?

What will come in place of (?) in the following number series?
15, 16, 24, 51, 115, ?
questions.explanation:
The difference between consecutive terms is cubes of consecutive integers:
• 16 − 15 = 1 (1³)
• 24 − 16 = 8 (2³)
• 51 − 24 = 27 (3³)
• 115 − 51 = 64 (4³)
• Next term = 115 + 5³ = 115 + 125 = 240.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².
